sources.page: GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Platinum Roadmap: All 55 Trophies
GTA 6 Trophy List: All 55 Trophies and Achievements
GTA VI trophies and achievements: the full official list
GTA 6 Trophy List: All 55 Trophies & Achievements
GTA 6 Trophy List: All 55 Trophies and Achievements

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned. There is no separate task: it is the sum of the whole guide. Plan the run in stages — story first (Chapters 1-5), then the 100% Completion checklist, then Strangers & Freaks and the miscellaneous cleanup — and the platinum lands on the last trophy you earn, whatever that is. PowerPyx rates the whole run 4/10 difficulty and about 200 hours; every trophy is offline and single-player, so nothing depends on servers or other players.
trophies.inShort: Earn the other 54 trophies and the platinum pops automatically.

steps.t: Follow the roadmap in order: Stage 1 story (Chapters 1-2), Stage 2 story (Chapters 3-4) plus contact missions, Stage 3 the final mission and the 100% checklist, Stage 4 cleanup.
Do the one possibly missable thing early: the Chapter 1 balcony meditation for Positive Mental Attitude, right after the mission Down to Earth.
Track everything in this app as you go: tick each trophy earned, use the counters for meditations, vehicles, WAiNK spots and challenges.
Finish A Long Road (100% Completion) before the last cleanup trophies: it is the longest single requirement and gates nothing else, but it takes the most hours.
Leave the easy one-off trophies (cocktail on Ocean Beach, bowling, scooter registrations) for the end: they pop in minutes and make a clean finish.
When 54 of 55 show earned here, the platinum is one trophy away: check the Next Up list for the cheapest remaining trophy.
Budget about 200 hours for the whole run at 4/10 difficulty: the checklist is long, not hard.
Everything is offline and single-player: no trophy depends on servers or other players.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Automatic story trophy: it pops when you finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing, in Chapter 1. You cannot miss it and there is nothing to prepare — just play the first mission through. Gone Fishing introduces Lucia and Jason and sets up the story, so it is the first trophy almost every player earns. If you are following the roadmap, this is Stage 1, step one.
trophies.inShort: Finish the opening mission Gone Fishing in Chapter 1.

steps.t: Start a new game and play the opening mission Gone Fishing through to its end.
The trophy pops automatically on mission completion: no extra objective is needed.
After it pops, stay in Chapter 1 for the missable balcony meditation before moving on (see Positive Mental Attitude).
Use the opening missions to learn the controls: driving, shooting and switching between Lucia and Jason all matter later.
Scan the first vehicles you drive with WAiNK: the vehicle log starts counting from the very first car.
Do not rush past the opening area: the first fishing spot and the first activity introductions are all in Chapter 1.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Automatic story trophy: it pops when you finish Chapter 1. Play every Chapter 1 main mission in order; side content is optional at this point. The important thing is what happens BEFORE Chapter 1 ends: the balcony meditation at Jason's house (after the mission Down to Earth) is the game's one possibly missable interaction, so do it before the chapter closes. Once Paradise Lost pops, that meditation is gone for the playthrough.
trophies.inShort: Finish Chapter 1 — but do the balcony meditation first.

steps.t: Play the Chapter 1 main missions in order until the chapter ends.
Before the final Chapter 1 mission: after Down to Earth, find Lucia in the kitchen at Jason's house in the morning, follow her to the balcony and accept the meditation.
Check the meditation counter under Progress > Collections > Exploration > Meditations: the balcony visit should show as 1.
Finish the chapter: Paradise Lost pops on completion, and the balcony meditation can no longer be done.
After Chapter 1, confirm the meditation counter reads at least 1: if it reads 0, the balcony was missed.
Start Chapter 2 with the WAiNK habit: scan every unfamiliar vehicle and animal you pass.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Automatic story trophy: it pops when you finish Chapter 2. Chapter 2 is where the game opens up: after the mission Coffee Break you can play as both Lucia and Jason, which is when most collectibles become doable with both characters. Use Chapter 2 to start the long counters — scanning vehicles with WAiNK, trying activities, and visiting the first meditation spots — while the story carries you through Leonida.
trophies.inShort: Finish Chapter 2; both characters unlock after Coffee Break.

steps.t: Play the Chapter 2 main missions in order.
After the mission Coffee Break, both characters are playable: switch freely to double up meditation spots and activities.
Start the long counters now: scan vehicles with WAiNK, try each activity type once, and visit meditation spots with both characters.
Finish the chapter: the trophy pops on completion.
After Chapter 2, visit the first two meditation spots with both characters: Smooth Sand and Swamp are the closest.
Try the shooting range in Chapter 2: the 42 gold medals take a long time, so start early.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Automatic story trophy: it pops when you finish Chapter 3. By now Vice City itself is fully open and most side systems are available — contact missions, stranger strands, robberies and the full activity list. Keep the story moving, but take the contact missions as they appear: the final missions for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each carry their own trophy, and doing them when offered is the simplest way to keep the roadmap clean.
trophies.inShort: Finish Chapter 3; take contact missions as they appear.

steps.t: Play the Chapter 3 main missions in order.
Accept contact missions as they appear: each contact's final mission is its own trophy (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone).
Use the open map to start collectible sweeps between missions: WAiNK scans, vehicles to discover, and meditation spots.
Visit the first meditation spots with the character you have: the others wait until both characters unlock.
Try the shooting range and the arcades when you pass them: both are activity types for Master of None.
Finish the chapter: the trophy pops on completion.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Automatic story trophy: it pops when you finish Chapter 4. Chapter 4 is the last full chapter before the finale, and by its end you should have most of the long counters well underway: stunts, shooting range medals, races and robberies. There is still free-roam after the story with no mission replay, so anything not finished by the finale stays available in the open world — except the Chapter 1 meditation, which is long gone by now.
trophies.inShort: Finish Chapter 4; long counters should be well underway.

steps.t: Play the Chapter 4 main missions in order.
Check the long counters before the finale: stunts, shooting range golds, drone races, races won, bank vaults and gang operations.
Finish any contact mission strands still open: their final missions are separate trophies.
Stock up before the finale: ammo, armor and a fast getaway car all matter in the last missions.
Check the shooting range golds before the finale: the range is open now and the 42 golds take time.
Finish the chapter: the trophy pops on completion.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Gold story trophy: it pops when you finish the final mission of the game. The story runs five chapters and takes roughly 60-80 hours, and the final mission closes it. After the story you return to the open world in free-roam, and the 100% Completion checklist becomes viewable under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion. Nothing in the finale is missable, and there are no mission gold medals to chase — just finish the mission.
trophies.inShort: Finish the final story mission (gold).

steps.t: Complete Chapters 1-4 and the missions leading into the finale.
Play the final mission through: the gold trophy pops on completion.
After the story, open Progress > Stats > 100% Completion to see the checklist that gates A Long Road.
Continue in free-roam: everything except the Chapter 1 meditation is still available.
Save before the final mission: a manual save lets you replay the finale for fun without touching the checklist.
After the finale, the 100% checklist is the roadmap: work it block by block, starting with challenges.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Automatic mission trophy: it pops when you complete the mission Breakfast Run. Breakfast Run is an early Chapter 1 mission, so this is one of the first trophies you will earn after the opening. Play it in story order; there is no special requirement and nothing to prepare. The mission's name is also the first hint that the game tracks your choices — but Trust itself only needs the mission finished.
trophies.inShort: Complete the mission Breakfast Run.

steps.t: Play the story until the mission Breakfast Run appears in Chapter 1.
Complete Breakfast Run: the trophy pops on mission completion.
Keep playing Chapter 1 in order toward Paradise Lost.
After Breakfast Run, the story opens up: use the freedom to try fishing and the other early activities.
Watch for the mission Down to Earth: it is the trigger for the missable balcony meditation.
Note the mission for later: the game's choice tracking (see Actions Speak Louder) starts counting from missions like this one.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Automatic mission trophy: it pops when you complete the mission The Cartel Heist. The Cartel Heist is a Chapter 2 story mission, so just follow the story until it appears and finish it. It is also good practice for the robbery trophies later — bank vaults, armored trucks and gang operations all use the same rhythm of planning, execution and escape that this heist teaches.
trophies.inShort: Complete the mission The Cartel Heist.

steps.t: Play the story until the mission The Cartel Heist appears in Chapter 2.
Complete The Cartel Heist: the trophy pops on mission completion.
Treat it as robbery practice: the same plan-execute-escape rhythm applies to Maximum Withdrawal, A Classic Blitz Play and Pest Control.
Keep the story moving toward Chapter 3.
After the heist, try a gang operation: the robbery skills transfer directly.
Bank the heist money before big purchases: garages and car mods are the next big spends.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Automatic mission trophy: it pops when you complete the mission Child's Play. Child's Play is a Chapter 3 story mission, so follow the story until it appears and finish it. There is no extra requirement. By Chapter 3 the game is fully open, so if any side content has been waiting — contact missions, stranger strands, the first collectible sweeps — this is a good point in the story to clear some of it between missions.
trophies.inShort: Complete the mission Child's Play.

steps.t: Play the story until the mission Child's Play appears in Chapter 3.
Complete Child's Play: the trophy pops on mission completion.
Between missions, clear waiting side content: contact missions and stranger strands keep the roadmap clean.
Keep the story moving toward Chapter 4.
In Chapter 3, try the bowling alley: it is one activity type and a trophy of its own.
Start the vehicle hunt in Chapter 3: Vice City's streets hold the rarest cars.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Automatic mission trophy: it pops when you complete the mission Headliners. Headliners is a Chapter 3 story mission. Play it in story order and finish it — no preparation needed. The mission's name is spelled DWNFALL in the trophy list, exactly as PlayStation publishes it; the list keeps the stylized spelling, and so does this guide.
trophies.inShort: Complete the mission Headliners.

steps.t: Play the story until the mission Headliners appears in Chapter 3.
Complete Headliners: the trophy pops on mission completion.
Note the spelling: the trophy is listed as DWNFALL, matching the official list.
Keep the story moving toward Chapter 4.
After Headliners, check the stranger markers: Chapter 3 is when most stranger strands open.
Try a drone race in Chapter 3: Top Fun locations are spread across the map and a win counts early.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Automatic mission trophy: it pops when you complete the mission VCIA Takedown. VCIA is the Vice City International Airport, and the takedown is a Chapter 3 story mission. Finish it in story order. The airport comes back later for the trophy Catch Me If You Can — an unscheduled departure from VCIA — so remember the layout: runways, terminals and the roads out are worth knowing when you plan that escape.
trophies.inShort: Complete the mission VCIA Takedown.

steps.t: Play the story until the mission VCIA Takedown appears in Chapter 3.
Complete VCIA Takedown: the trophy pops on mission completion.
Learn the airport layout while you are there: it matters later for Catch Me If You Can.
Keep the story moving toward Chapter 4.
Note the runway entrances while you are at VCIA: the unscheduled departure needs a fast way onto the airfield.
After the takedown, the airport stays open: planes can be stolen there any time in free-roam.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Automatic mission trophy: it pops when you complete the mission Operation Savage Glory. Operation Savage Glory is a Chapter 4 story mission. Play it in story order and finish it. Chapter 4 is the last full chapter before the finale, so after this mission, check the long counters — stunts, shooting range medals, races and robberies — before the final mission closes the story.
trophies.inShort: Complete the mission Operation Savage Glory.

steps.t: Play the story until the mission Operation Savage Glory appears in Chapter 4.
Complete Operation Savage Glory: the trophy pops on mission completion.
Before the finale, check the long counters: stunts, shooting range golds, drone races, races won, bank vaults, gang operations.
Finish any open contact strands, then move to the final mission.
After Operation Savage Glory, the story is nearly done: save the game before the finale.
Use the pause before the finale to sweep the nearest collectibles: cards and WAiNK spots near the story path.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Gold trophy, and the hardest single requirement in the game: reach 100% Completion on the in-game checklist. The checklist becomes viewable after the story, under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion, and it has 35 tasks. The thresholds are lenient — it is closer to 60% true game completion — but the hours are real: roughly 100 of the 200-hour platinum run go here. The big blocks are the story itself, 70 of 80 challenges, 15 of 18 meditations, 200 of 277 vehicles scanned, 100 of 255 animals studied, 39 gang operations, 22 bank jobs, 7 payday loan jobs, 8 bank vault robberies, 15 card sets, 100 WAiNK locations, 33 underwater discoveries and 100 Cocaine Flamingos. Track every block in this app's counters as you go.
trophies.inShort: Reach 100% on the 35-task checklist (gold, the longest grind).

steps.t: Finish the story first: the checklist is not viewable until after the final mission.
Open Progress > Stats > 100% Completion and read all 35 tasks: the checklist is the only authority on what counts.
Work the big blocks in parallel: 70 of 80 challenges, 15 of 18 meditations, 200 of 277 vehicles scanned with WAiNK, 100 of 255 animals studied through binoculars.
Clear the robbery blocks: 39 gang operations, 22 bank jobs, 7 payday loan jobs and 8 bank vault robberies.
Clear the collectible blocks: 15 card sets, 100 WAiNK locations, 33 underwater discoveries, 100 Cocaine Flamingos.
When the checklist reads 100%, A Long Road pops: the gold is the gateway to the platinum.
Work the checklist in county order: finish one county's blocks before moving to the next.
The last tasks are usually the grinds: 70 of 80 challenges and the final card sets take the longest.

dispute.q: How many tasks is the 100% checklist, and how strict is it?
dispute.a: 35 tasks, and lenient: about 60% true completion is enough.
dispute.b: Some lists count the checklist differently and warn the thresholds are stricter than they look.
dispute.call: Same move either way: follow the in-game checklist under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion — it is the only count the game itself uses.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Silver trophy: complete 250 stunts across Leonida. Stunts are the game's driving tricks — jumps, near misses, drifts, airtime — and they rack up naturally as you drive fast and recklessly through the story. 250 sounds like a lot, but a normal playthrough with spirited driving covers a large share; the remainder is a short cleanup of jumps and drifts in free-roam. Track the counter here and in the game's stats; there is no single best spot, so just drive hard everywhere and let the count climb.
trophies.inShort: Complete 250 stunts (silver).

steps.t: Drive aggressively from the start: jumps, drifts, near misses and airtime all count toward the 250.
Check the stunt count in the game stats regularly: most players cover a large share during the story alone.
In free-roam, chain stunts on highways and ramps: jumps and drifts are the fastest repeatable stunts.
Use fast cars and bikes for airtime: the longer the jump, the more the stunt is worth to the counter.
At 250 stunts the silver pops: tick it off here and move to the next counter.
Ramps and hills are the best stunt spots: a jump with a clean landing counts every time.
Near misses count too: threading traffic at speed is a stunt that needs no setup.

dispute.q: Do the 250 stunts have to be unique, or do repeats count?
dispute.a: Repeats count: the counter climbs on every stunt you perform.
dispute.b: Some early lists describe the requirement as 250 unique stunts.
dispute.call: Same move either way: keep performing stunts and watch the in-game counter — if repeats did not count, the counter would stall, and it does not.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: try each of the 9 activity types once. The nine types are the game's side activities — fishing, arcade games, the shooting range, drone races, races, bowling, hunting, meditation and one more rotating activity — and one try at each is enough. Most players earn this without trying, just by sampling everything as the story introduces it. If one type is still missing late in the game, check the list here: the untried type is the one to go and do once.
trophies.inShort: Try all 9 activity types once.

steps.t: Sample every activity as the story introduces it: fishing, arcade, shooting range, drone races, races, bowling, hunting, meditation.
Check which of the 9 types you have tried: this app lists them, and the game tracks them under activities.
Do the missing type once: a single fishing challenge, one arcade game, one drone race, one bowling game, one hunt, one meditation.
The trophy pops on the ninth type tried: no scores or wins are needed, just one attempt each.
The fastest way to nine types: fish once, play one arcade game, bowl one game, meditate once, win one drone race.
Hunting counts as a type too: Bret's strand covers it while you chase Fair Game.

dispute.q: Which 9 activity types count?
dispute.a: Fishing, arcade, shooting range, drone races, races, bowling, hunting, meditation, plus one rotating activity.
dispute.b: Some lists name the ninth type differently or split racing into two types.
dispute.call: Same move either way: try every activity the game offers once — the counter only needs nine, and sampling everything covers every reading.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Silver trophy: earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. The shooting range has 42 challenges, and every one needs gold — not just a pass. This is one of the hardest trophies on pure skill: steady aim, fast target acquisition and clean reloads. Practice each challenge until the gold threshold is comfortable, then run them in order and tick each gold off here. No other requirement gates it: the range is available from early in the game, so start early and chip away at it between missions.
trophies.inShort: Gold all 42 Shooting Range challenges (silver).

steps.t: Visit the shooting range early: all 42 challenges are available from early in the game.
Learn each challenge's gold threshold before trying in earnest: speed and accuracy both matter, and reloading wastes time.
Practice the hardest challenges first while your aim is fresh, then run the full set in order.
Use the weapon the challenge gives you: switching mid-challenge costs time and breaks the rhythm.
Tick each gold off here: at 42 of 42 the silver pops.
Warm up on the easy challenges: the gold thresholds are lower there and the rhythm carries over.
If a challenge keeps beating you, change your stance and sight picture before changing weapons.

dispute.q: Do all 42 challenges really need gold, or is a pass enough for some?
dispute.a: All 42 need gold: the trophy description says a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
dispute.b: A few early lists suggest some challenges only need completion.
dispute.call: Same move either way: gold every challenge — a pass on a challenge you later gold changes nothing, and gold is the only reading that matches the trophy text.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: win a Top Fun Drone Race at every one of the 14 locations. Top Fun runs drone races at 14 spots around Leonida, and a win at each is required — plus the 42 Drone Time Trials across the same 14 locations count toward 100% Completion, so the two goals share the same map. Learn each course's line, cut corners where the drone allows it, and win one race per location. The races are short, so a full sweep is a single focused session once you know the courses.
trophies.inShort: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations.

steps.t: Find the 14 Top Fun locations on the map: they are spread across Leonida, one race each.
Learn each course before racing it in earnest: the racing line and the corner cuts matter more than raw speed.
Win one race at each location: a win anywhere counts, and you can retry a location as often as needed.
While there, run the Drone Time Trials too: 42 trials across the same 14 locations count toward 100% Completion.
At 14 of 14 locations won, the trophy pops.
Race at low-traffic times in the game world: fewer obstacles on the course means cleaner lines.
Each location has three trials as well as the race: a location visit can clear four objectives at once.

dispute.q: Do the Drone Time Trials count toward Top Fun, or only the races?
dispute.a: Only race wins count for this trophy; the trials are a separate 100% requirement.
dispute.b: Some lists blur the two together as one Top Fun objective.
dispute.call: Same move either way: win a race at all 14 locations, then run the trials for 100% — doing both covers every reading.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: win 20 different races. Races are the game's driving competitions — street races, circuits and point-to-point runs around Leonida — and the trophy needs 20 different ones won, not the same race 20 times. Spread the wins across the map: each race has its own start, route and best car class, so vary the vehicle to suit the course. Wins stack up quickly once you know the routes, and the 20th different win pops the trophy.
trophies.inShort: Win 20 different races.

steps.t: Find races around Leonida: street circuits, point-to-point runs and class events all count.
Win a race, then move to a different one: the trophy needs 20 DIFFERENT races, not repeats.
Match the car to the course: tight city circuits want handling, open highways want top speed.
Learn each route before racing it flat out: a clean first lap beats a fast crash.
At 20 different races won, the trophy pops.
Races unlock across the map as you explore: new areas bring new races.
Upgrade the car for the course, not for top speed alone: brakes and grip win city circuits.

dispute.q: Which races count: any 20, or only specific race types?
dispute.a: Any 20 different races count, across all race types.
dispute.b: Some lists suggest only street races count, or that repeat wins on one race stack.
dispute.call: Same move either way: win 20 different races of any type — variety covers every reading, and repeats are worthless under both.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the game's fishing rival, and the challenge is a head-to-head fishing contest: catch more, or better, fish than he does in the time given. Fishing is one of the nine activity types, so this also ticks one off Master of None. Learn the fishing mechanics first — casting, reeling, tension — then challenge Cal and out-fish him. One win is enough.
trophies.inShort: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.

steps.t: Find the fishing spots and learn the mechanics: casting, reeling and keeping the line tension in the safe zone.
Challenge Cal to a fishing challenge when the option appears.
Out-fish him: more fish, or better fish, inside the time limit — steady reeling beats frantic reeling.
One win pops the trophy; repeat challenges are only for fun after that.
Fish at dawn or dusk in the game world: the bite rate is better and Cal is easier to beat.
Upgrade the rod and line if the shop offers them: better gear means fewer lost fish.

dispute.q: When can you challenge Cal: any time, or only at a set point?
dispute.a: The challenge is available once fishing is introduced and Cal is around.
dispute.b: Some lists tie the challenge to a specific story beat.
dispute.call: Same move either way: learn to fish, then take the challenge the first time Cal offers it — you cannot miss it by fishing first.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: complete an arcade game. The arcades around Leonida have playable machines, and finishing any one game — any machine, any result — pops the trophy. It is one of the easiest trophies in the list and one of the nine activity types for Master of None. Walk into an arcade, pick a machine, play it through to the end, and the trophy is yours.
trophies.inShort: Complete one arcade game.

steps.t: Find an arcade in Vice City or elsewhere in Leonida.
Pick any machine and play: any game counts, and the result does not matter.
Play the game through to its end: quitting early does not count as completing it.
The trophy pops on completion: one game is all it takes.
Pick a short game if you are in a hurry: any machine counts, so the quickest game is the fastest trophy.
Arcades also hide card packs and collectibles: look around the arcade before you leave.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: complete the final mission for Andy. Andy is one of the five contacts whose mission strands end in their own trophy (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone). Take Andy's missions as they appear in the open world and follow the strand to its final mission. Contact strands are not story missions, so they can be done between chapters; just do not leave them all to the end, or the finale stretch gets crowded.
trophies.inShort: Complete Andy's final mission.

steps.t: Meet Andy and take his first mission when it appears in the open world.
Follow Andy's strand mission by mission: each one leads to the next.
Complete Andy's final mission: the trophy pops on completion.
Do the same for the other four contacts: Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have their own final-mission trophy.
Andy's strand pays well: the mission rewards fund the next garage purchase.
Check the contact list after Andy's finale: a new strand may open in the same area.

dispute.q: Can a contact's final mission be missed if you ignore the strand?
dispute.a: No: contact strands stay available in free-roam after the story.
dispute.b: Some early lists warn that contacts can become unavailable late in the game.
dispute.call: Same move either way: do each contact's strand as it appears instead of leaving all five to the end.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: complete the final mission for Kenton. Kenton is one of the five contacts with a final-mission trophy. Follow his strand through the open world to its last mission and finish it. The title is a joke about the mission itself — play it and the joke lands. Like the other contact trophies, it is safest to do Kenton's strand as it appears rather than saving all five for after the story.
trophies.inShort: Complete Kenton's final mission.

steps.t: Meet Kenton and take his first mission when it appears.
Follow Kenton's strand mission by mission to its final mission.
Complete Kenton's final mission: the trophy pops on completion.
Clear the remaining contacts (Andy, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) the same way.
Kenton's missions are boat-heavy: keep a fast boat ready near the coast.
The boat missions double as exploration: the coast holds WAiNK spots and card packs.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: complete the final mission for Billy. Billy is one of the five contacts with a final-mission trophy. His strand runs through the open world, and its last mission pops the trophy. Billy's missions lean on bikes and solo rides — the trophy's name is the hint — so keep a fast bike handy while you work through his strand.
trophies.inShort: Complete Billy's final mission.

steps.t: Meet Billy and take his first mission when it appears.
Follow Billy's strand mission by mission to its final mission.
Keep a fast bike ready: Billy's missions lean on solo riding.
Complete Billy's final mission: the trophy pops on completion.
Billy's strand is the best bike practice in the game: the riding skills transfer to races.
After Billy's finale, the bike stays useful: stunts and races both favor two wheels.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Silver trophy: complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida. Strangers & Freaks are the game's oddball side characters — each one has a short strand of missions, and eight completed strands pop the silver. There are more than eight strangers in Leonida, so you can pick the eight whose strands you like best; the rest are optional. Strands appear as question marks and encounters around the map, so explore widely and take every stranger mission you find.
trophies.inShort: Complete 8 stranger mission strands (silver).

steps.t: Explore Leonida widely: stranger encounters appear as markers around the map.
Take every stranger mission you find: each strand is short, usually two or three missions.
Finish a strand completely before moving on: a half-finished strand does not count toward the eight.
Count your completed strands here: at 8 the silver pops, and the remaining strangers are optional.
If a stranger seems stuck, move on and come back later: some strands need story progress to continue.
Strangers cluster in Vice City and the countryside towns: sweep both and you will find eight quickly.
Each strand pays in cash and items: the rewards fund garage purchases and car mods.

dispute.q: Which 8 stranger strands count: any 8, or a fixed set?
dispute.a: Any 8 completed strands count: there are more strangers than the trophy needs.
dispute.b: Some lists name a fixed set of eight qualifying strangers.
dispute.call: Same move either way: complete eight strands, any eight — if a fixed set existed, completing eight strands would still include it once you do them all.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: complete the final mission for Randy. Randy is one of the five contacts with a final-mission trophy. Follow his strand through the open world to its last mission and finish it. Randy's strand is about supply runs and deals — the trophy's name is the business model — so expect driving, deliveries and the occasional shootout on the way to the final mission.
trophies.inShort: Complete Randy's final mission.

steps.t: Meet Randy and take his first mission when it appears.
Follow Randy's strand mission by mission to its final mission.
Complete Randy's final mission: the trophy pops on completion.
Clear the remaining contacts (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Tyrone) the same way.
Randy's strand is about supply runs: the driving practice helps the race trophies later.
Supply runs pay in marked bills: launder them through a contact for Dime on the Dollar.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: complete the final mission for Tyrone. Tyrone is the last of the five contacts with a final-mission trophy. Follow his strand through the open world to its last mission and finish it. Once all five contact trophies are done — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone — the side-mission half of the roadmap is clean, and only the stranger strands and the long counters remain.
trophies.inShort: Complete Tyrone's final mission.

steps.t: Meet Tyrone and take his first mission when it appears.
Follow Tyrone's strand mission by mission to its final mission.
Complete Tyrone's final mission: the trophy pops on completion.
Check the other four contacts are done: all five final-mission trophies together clear the contact half of the roadmap.
Tyrone's finale is the last contact trophy: five contacts, five trophies, one clean block of the roadmap.
After all five contacts, the stranger strands are the remaining side content: eight strands for the silver.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy, and the only possibly missable trophy in the game: meditate at every spot across Leonida. There are 18 meditations across 10 spots: most spots count once per character, so Jason and Lucia each meditate at the same spot for 2; Jason's House counts 1, and Ascent Mountain counts 1. Only 15 of 18 are needed for 100% Completion, but this trophy needs all 18. The trap is the first one: after the Chapter 1 mission Down to Earth, Lucia invites Jason to meditate on the balcony at Jason's house — accept immediately, because that meditation disappears when Chapter 1 ends, and whether the trophy needs it is unconfirmed. Both characters are playable after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, so the other 9 spots can be done with both. Track progress under Progress > Collections > Exploration > Meditations, and use the counter here.
trophies.inShort: Meditate at all 18 spots — do the Chapter 1 balcony first, it can be missed.

steps.t: CHAPTER 1 ONLY: after the mission Down to Earth, find Lucia in the kitchen at Jason's house in the morning, follow her to the balcony and accept the meditation. Do this before Chapter 1 ends.
Check the counter under Progress > Collections > Exploration > Meditations: the balcony visit should read 1.
After the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, both characters are playable: visit each of the other 9 spots with both Jason and Lucia for 2 meditations each.

The 9 spots: Smooth Sand (sandbar west of Capri), Swamp (Buckskin Swamp dock), Worn Stone (Camp Moonflower), Red Rocks (Manifest Canyon), Water Wheel (paper mill, south Moreau), Jutting Cliff (Mount Kalaga), Waterfall (north-west of Tallaloko), Seaside (rocky beach, Leonard County), and Ascent Mountain last.
Ascent Mountain unlocks only after the other spots are done: it is the final meditation, at the stone circle on Mount Kalaga's peak.
Meditate with each character at each spot: spots are marked with a purple icon on the map when you go near them.
At 18 of 18 the trophy pops. If you skipped the balcony, finish the other 17 and see whether the final meditation still takes you to 18.
The two hardest spots to reach are Jutting Cliff and Ascent Mountain: both are on Mount Kalaga, so climb once and do both.
Do the Waterfall spot last before Ascent Mountain: it is the farthest north-west and the easiest to leave behind.

dispute.q: Does the Chapter 1 balcony meditation count toward the trophy?
dispute.a: Yes: it raises the counter by 1, and the trophy needs every spot.
dispute.b: Unproven: the balcony is not marked as a standard spot, and the final meditation may count double so the total still reaches 18 without it.
dispute.call: Same move either way: do the balcony meditation in Chapter 1. It costs two minutes and covers every reading; skipping it is a gamble on an unconfirmed theory.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret is a hunting contact who wants one specific animal — a unique specimen, not just any animal of the species. Follow Bret's strand to the hunt: track the animal, get close without spooking it, and take the shot cleanly. Hunting is also one of the nine activity types, and studying animals through binoculars counts toward 100% Completion (100 of 255 animals), so the hunt doubles as progress on the checklist.
trophies.inShort: Hunt the unique animal for Bret.

steps.t: Meet Bret and take his hunting strand when it appears.
Follow the strand to the unique animal's territory: track it by its signs and calls.
Approach without spooking it: move slowly, stay downwind, and use cover.
Take the shot cleanly and collect the animal: the trophy pops on the successful hunt.
While hunting, study animals through binoculars: 100 of 255 studied counts toward 100% Completion.
Hunt at dawn: the unique animal is most active then and the light is better for the shot.
Bring a scoped rifle: the unique animal is wary and the shot is usually long.

dispute.q: Which animal is the unique one for Bret?
dispute.a: A single named specimen tied to Bret's strand — the strand itself points you to it.
dispute.b: Some lists name a specific animal and location, and the names disagree.
dispute.call: Same move either way: follow Bret's strand — it leads to the animal whatever the lists call it.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Silver trophy: complete 3 Collectible Card sets. Collectible cards are scattered around Leonida in packs, and a set is complete when you hold every card in it. Three complete sets pop the silver; 100% Completion wants 15 sets, so this trophy is the early milestone on a longer hunt. Cards are found in the world — shops, interiors, hidden spots — so sweep each area as you explore it rather than saving all card hunting for the end.
trophies.inShort: Complete 3 Collectible Card sets (silver).

steps.t: Pick up every card pack you see while exploring: cards are scattered in shops, interiors and hidden spots.
Check your collection under Progress > Collections to see which sets are close to complete.
Finish the three easiest sets first: small sets complete faster than big ones.
At 3 complete sets the silver pops; keep collecting toward the 15 sets that 100% Completion wants.
Sweep each area for cards as you explore it: backtracking for one missing card is the slow way.
Shops and interiors hide the most packs: check every shop counter and back room.
Trade duplicates if the game allows it: a duplicate is worth more in a trade than in a drawer.

dispute.q: Which card sets count: any 3, or specific ones?
dispute.a: Any 3 complete sets count.
dispute.b: Some lists suggest only certain sets count toward the trophy.
dispute.call: Same move either way: complete any three sets — the counter only needs three, and finishing more sets never hurts.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Silver trophy: WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK is the in-game app for scanning the world — point it at vehicles, animals and landmarks and it logs them. 100 WAiNK locations are needed here, and the same app covers the 100% Completion requirements (200 of 277 vehicles scanned, 100 of 255 animals studied), so every scan does double duty. Make WAiNK a habit: scan everything unfamiliar as you travel, and the 100 comes without a dedicated grind.
trophies.inShort: WAiNK It at 100 locations (silver).

steps.t: Open the WAiNK app and learn the scan: point it at vehicles, animals and landmarks.
Scan everything unfamiliar as you travel: every scan counts toward the 100 and toward 100% Completion.
Scan vehicles especially: 200 of 277 base model vehicles scanned is a separate 100% block.
Study animals through binoculars too: 100 of 255 studied is another 100% block.
At 100 WAiNK locations the silver pops.
Scan landmarks as well as vehicles: a landmark scan counts the same as any other scan.
Pair WAiNK with driving: scan every new vehicle you climb into and the 100 arrives on its own.

dispute.q: What counts as a WAiNK location: any scan, or only landmarks?
dispute.a: Any WAiNK scan counts toward the 100.
dispute.b: Some lists say only landmark scans count, not vehicles or animals.
dispute.call: Same move either way: scan everything — landmarks, vehicles and animals — and the counter climbs under every reading.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: complete 50 challenges. The game has 80 challenges in eight groups of ten, and this trophy needs any 50 of them. 100% Completion needs 70 of 80, so this trophy is the halfway mark on the same road. Challenges cover everything — driving, shooting, flying, collectibles, crime — so play widely and the count climbs on its own. Pick the easy groups first (the ones that match how you already play), then grind the rest for 100%.
trophies.inShort: Complete 50 challenges (70 of 80 needed for 100%).

steps.t: Open the challenges list and read the eight groups of ten: driving, shooting, flying, collectibles, crime and more.
Play widely: challenges complete themselves as you drive, shoot, fly and collect.
Pick the easy groups first: the ones that match how you already play finish fastest.
At 50 challenges the trophy pops; keep going to 70 of 80 for 100% Completion.
Track the count here and in the game: the last ten challenges are the grind, so save them for the cleanup stage.
The driving and shooting groups are the easiest to complete: they reward what you already do.
Save the flying challenges for last: they need the most practice and the best aircraft.

dispute.q: Which 50 challenges count: any 50, or a fixed set?
dispute.a: Any 50 of the 80 count.
dispute.b: Some lists imply specific challenge groups are required.
dispute.call: Same move either way: complete any 50 — and since 100% needs 70, you will do most of them anyway.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat. You need your partner beside you, a 4-star wanted level, and a clean escape. The recipe: bring your partner along, commit crimes until the wanted level hits 4 stars, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear — without your partner getting caught or going down. Fast cars, alleyways and the countryside all work for the escape; the hard part is keeping your partner with you through it.
trophies.inShort: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner beside you.

steps.t: Bring your partner along: the trophy needs both of you together when the heat breaks.
Commit crimes until the wanted level reaches 4 stars: robberies, shootouts and chases all raise it.
Break line of sight: lose the pursuing cops, then stay out of their view until the stars clear.
Keep your partner alive and with you through the escape: if they go down or get caught, the attempt fails.
When the wanted level clears with your partner beside you, the trophy pops.
Use the countryside for the escape: open roads and few cops make the heat easier to lose.
Do not use a slow vehicle for the escape: speed is what breaks the line of sight.

dispute.q: Does your partner have to be in the same vehicle, or just nearby?
dispute.a: Nearby is enough: the trophy checks your partner is with you when the heat clears.
dispute.b: Some lists say your partner must be in your vehicle for the whole escape.
dispute.call: Same move either way: keep your partner in your vehicle for the escape — it satisfies both readings.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level. The trick is in the wording: you must KEEP your wanted level through all three robberies — losing the heat between shops breaks the chain. Bring your partner, rob a shop, move straight to the next shop while the cops are still after you, rob it, then the third, all without the wanted level clearing. Plan a route with three close shops, keep the getaway car ready, and do not stop to fight the police between robberies.
trophies.inShort: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, wanted level unbroken.

steps.t: Bring your partner and pick a route with three shops close together.
Rob the first shop with your partner: the wanted level rises — that is what you want.
Move straight to the second shop while the wanted level is still active: do NOT lose the heat between shops.
Rob the second shop, then the third, still with the wanted level unbroken.
After the third robbery the trophy pops: then lose the heat however you like.
Plan the route before the first robbery: three shops on one street make the chain easy.
Keep the getaway car parked facing the exit: every second counts when the heat is on.

dispute.q: Does the wanted level have to stay up the whole time, or just never hit zero?
dispute.a: It has to stay up: losing the heat between shops breaks the chain of three.
dispute.b: Some lists read it as three robberies in one session regardless of the heat.
dispute.call: Same move either way: keep the wanted level alive through all three robberies — it satisfies both readings.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: discover 100 vehicles. Discovering means finding a vehicle type you have not seen before — driving it, or scanning it with WAiNK, logs it. There are 277 base model vehicles in the game, and 100% Completion wants 200 of them scanned, so this trophy is the halfway mark on the same hunt. Drive everything you see, scan unfamiliar vehicles with WAiNK as you travel, and check the vehicle list under Progress to see what is still missing.
trophies.inShort: Discover 100 vehicles.

steps.t: Drive every vehicle you see: entering a new type logs it as discovered.
Scan unfamiliar vehicles with WAiNK as you travel: scans log vehicles too.
Check the vehicle list under Progress to see which types are still missing.
Hunt the rare types in their home areas: sports cars in Vice City, off-roaders in the countryside, boats on the water.
At 100 vehicles discovered the trophy pops; keep going to 200 scanned for 100% Completion.
Check car meets and docks: the rare types gather where enthusiasts do.
Aircraft and boats count as vehicles too: the list is not just cars.

dispute.q: Does discovering mean driving it, scanning it, or either?
dispute.a: Either: driving a new type or scanning it with WAiNK both log it.
dispute.b: Some lists say only driving counts, or only scanning counts.
dispute.call: Same move either way: drive it AND scan it — doing both logs the vehicle under every reading.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-motion aiming mode: trigger it in a firefight with at least five enemies in view, and drop all five before the focus ends. The setup matters more than the aim: find a fight with a crowd of enemies, let them group up, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them head by head. A shotgun or automatic weapon helps — five quick takedowns inside one focus window is the whole trick.
trophies.inShort: Down 5 enemies in one Combat Focus.

steps.t: Find a firefight with at least five enemies: gang operations and police chases are the best crowds.
Let the enemies group up before triggering Combat Focus: spread-out targets waste the window.
Trigger Combat Focus and take down five enemies before it ends: headshots drop them fastest.
Use a shotgun or automatic weapon: five quick takedowns need firepower, not precision.
If you only get four, retry: the trophy needs all five inside one single use.
Gang operations are the best setup: the enemies arrive in waves and group naturally.
Trigger the focus when the enemies are close together: the window is short and grouping is everything.

dispute.q: Does the focus window end on a timer, or when you stop shooting?
dispute.a: It runs on a timer: five takedowns must land inside one window.
dispute.b: Some lists describe the window as ending when you release the trigger.
dispute.call: Same move either way: drop five fast in one burst — speed satisfies both readings.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: make an unscheduled departure at VCIA. VCIA is the Vice City International Airport, and an unscheduled departure means leaving by air without a ticket — steal a plane and take off. Get onto the airfield, find a plane on the runway or apron, get in, and take off while the airport security and police react. You do not need to fly far: getting airborne from VCIA without authorization is the departure, and the trophy pops once you are up.
trophies.inShort: Steal a plane and take off from VCIA.

steps.t: Get to VCIA, the Vice City International Airport: the airfield is the target.
Find a plane on the runway or apron: small planes are easiest to steal.
Get in and take off: airport security and police will react, so be quick.
Once you are airborne from VCIA, the trophy pops: you do not need to fly anywhere in particular.
If security stops you on the ground, retry: the attempt only counts once you are up.
Enter the airfield at night: security is thinner and the planes are still parked.
A small plane is the fastest steal: it needs less runway and takes off sooner.

dispute.q: Does any aircraft count, or only planes?
dispute.a: Any aircraft that gets you airborne from VCIA counts.
dispute.b: Some lists say only fixed-wing planes count, not helicopters.
dispute.call: Same move either way: steal a plane — it satisfies both readings.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: kinda hot in these Rhinos. Rhinos are the game's tanks, and the trophy is about dealing with them — surviving their attention, or turning their firepower to your use. The practical route is a high wanted level: at 4-5 stars the military rolls in with Rhinos, and the trophy tracks your interaction with them. Get a tank's attention, survive the encounter, and the trophy pops. Heavy weapons and distance help: a Rhino's cannon does not miss twice.
trophies.inShort: Deal with the Rhinos (tanks) at high wanted levels.

steps.t: Raise your wanted level to 4-5 stars: the military responds with Rhinos.
Find the Rhino when it arrives: it is slow, loud and impossible to miss.
Survive its attention: keep distance, use cover, and do not let its cannon line up on you twice.
Use heavy weapons if you have them: explosives and the minigun are the practical answers to armor.
The trophy pops on the Rhino encounter: the exact interaction the game tracks is surviving its fire.
If you can, destroy the Rhino as well: the lists disagree on the trigger, and destroying it covers the other reading.
A high wanted level in the countryside gives you room to maneuver: the city is a death trap against a tank.

dispute.q: What exactly triggers it: surviving a Rhino, destroying one, or driving one?
dispute.a: Surviving a Rhino encounter at a high wanted level triggers it.
dispute.b: Some lists say you must destroy a Rhino, or drive one yourself.
dispute.call: Same move either way: survive the encounter and, if you can, destroy the Rhino too — both readings are covered.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: rob a jewelry store without being detected. Pick a jewelry store, get in and out with the loot, and never trip the alarm or get spotted. The approach matters more than speed: case the store first, learn the guard patrols and camera angles, enter when the floor is quiet, take the jewelry, and leave before anyone notices. A detected robbery is just a normal robbery — this trophy needs a ghost run.
trophies.inShort: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.

steps.t: Pick a jewelry store and case it first: guard patrols, camera angles and exits.
Enter when the floor is quiet: fewer staff and customers means fewer eyes.
Take the jewelry without tripping the alarm: move slowly and avoid the cameras.
Leave before anyone notices: if the alarm trips or a guard spots you, the attempt fails — retry.
A clean, undetected robbery pops the trophy on exit.
Case the store in the daytime and rob it at night: the floor is quieter after closing time.
Disable or avoid the cameras first: a camera you never trigger is a camera that never sees you.

dispute.q: Which jewelry store counts: any, or a specific one?
dispute.a: Any jewelry store counts, as long as the robbery is undetected.
dispute.b: Some lists name one specific store in Vice City.
dispute.call: Same move either way: rob any jewelry store cleanly — a specific store is still a jewelry store.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Silver trophy: rob 5 bank vaults and escape. Bank vaults are the big robberies: get into the vault, take the cash, and get out with the police behind you. Five vaults, each with its own escape, pop the silver — and 100% Completion wants 8 bank vault robberies, so this is the early milestone. Plan each vault like a heist: entry, vault, exit route, getaway car. The escape is the hard part; the vault itself is just the middle.
trophies.inShort: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape (silver).

steps.t: Find the banks with vaults: five vaults are needed here, eight for 100% Completion.
Plan each vault like a heist: entry route, vault approach, exit route, getaway car staged nearby.
Rob the vault and escape: the trophy needs the escape, not just the robbery.
Lose the heat after each vault before starting the next: a clean escape keeps the chain simple.
At 5 vaults robbed and escaped the silver pops; keep going to 8 for 100% Completion.
The vaults pay in Marked Bills: launder them through a contact for Dime on the Dollar.
Vary the banks: five different vaults cover the lists that name specific banks.

dispute.q: Which banks have vaults: any bank, or only five specific ones?
dispute.a: Any five bank vaults count.
dispute.b: Some lists name specific banks and say others do not count.
dispute.call: Same move either way: rob five different bank vaults — variety covers every reading.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida, and robbing one means stopping it, breaking it open, taking the cash and getting away. The name is a nod to the classic GTA heist style: block the truck, breach it, grab the money, escape. Trucks are easiest on quiet roads where you can block them without traffic in the way; the escape is the same drill as every robbery — break line of sight and stay hidden until the heat clears.
trophies.inShort: Rob an armored truck and escape.

steps.t: Find an armored truck on its route: they drive set roads around Leonida.
Stop the truck on a quiet stretch: block it with a vehicle so it cannot drive on.
Break the truck open and take the cash: explosives or heavy weapons breach it fastest.
Escape with the money: break line of sight and stay hidden until the wanted level clears.
The trophy pops on a successful robbery and escape.
Trucks run on set routes: learn one route and wait for the truck instead of chasing it.
The cash is Marked Bills: launder it through a contact for Dime on the Dollar.

dispute.q: Do armored trucks spawn on a schedule, or only at set places?
dispute.a: They drive set routes: find a route and wait, or follow one.
dispute.b: Some lists say trucks only appear after story progress.
dispute.call: Same move either way: patrol the truck routes in free-roam — they run regardless of which reading is right.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: explore all of Leonida. Leonida has 52 named areas, and this trophy needs all of them visited — every county, city district, town and landmark zone on the map. The story takes you through most of them naturally, but the far corners (the Keys, the swamps, the northern counties) need a deliberate sweep. Use the map: an area counts when you enter it, and the game tracks the total under exploration. A full map sweep in free-roam, county by county, closes the last gaps.
trophies.inShort: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida.

steps.t: Play the story: it takes you through most of Leonida's 52 areas naturally.
Open the map and check which areas are still unvisited: the game tracks exploration by area.
Sweep the far corners deliberately: the Keys, the swamps and the northern counties are the usual gaps.
Drive, fly or sail into each missing area: entering it is enough to count it.
At 52 of 52 areas explored the trophy pops.
The Keys need a boat or a plane: the southern islands are not reachable by road alone.
Pair the exploration sweep with the collectible sweep: the same routes cover areas, cards and WAiNK spots.

dispute.q: What counts as an area: 52 named zones, or every map region?
dispute.a: 52 named areas: the game's own exploration count uses 52.
dispute.b: Some lists count a different total of map regions.
dispute.call: Same move either way: visit every named area on the map — the game's counter is the authority, and it reads 52.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang. Leonida has 9 gangs, each running illegal operations — drug labs, chop shops, smuggling runs — and this trophy needs one operation robbed from each of the nine. Gang operations are also a 100% Completion block (39 operations), so this trophy is the first nine of a longer count. Hit a different gang each time: the trophy tracks gangs, not operations, so nine operations against one gang only counts once.
trophies.inShort: Rob one illegal operation from each of the 9 gangs.

steps.t: Find gang operations on the map: each gang marks its territory and its operations.
Rob an operation from one gang, then move to a different gang: the trophy tracks gangs, not operations.
Work through all 9 gangs: one operation each is enough for this trophy.
Keep robbing operations after the trophy: 39 operations count toward 100% Completion.
At 9 of 9 gangs hit the trophy pops.
Operations pay in Marked Bills: launder them for Dime on the Dollar.
Mark each gang as you hit it: the counter tracks gangs, so one per gang is the plan.

dispute.q: Which 9 gangs count, and what is an illegal operation?
dispute.a: The nine gangs of Leonida, and their marked illegal operations: labs, chop shops, smuggling runs.
dispute.b: Some lists name the gangs differently or count operations differently.
dispute.call: Same move either way: rob one marked operation per gang, all nine — the map marks both the gangs and their operations.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is the game's quiet joke of a trophy: go to a bar on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and enjoy the view. No combat, no timer, no skill — just a drink with a view. Ocean Beach is the Vice City beachfront, and the bars along it serve the cocktail. Sit, order, and the trophy pops while you watch the ocean.
trophies.inShort: Have a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.

steps.t: Go to Ocean Beach on the Vice City beachfront.
Find a bar along the beachfront that serves cocktails.
Order a cocktail and enjoy it with the ocean view: no rush, no enemies.
The trophy pops as you drink: the easiest trophy in the game.
If the first bar does not trigger it, try the next one along the beachfront: any Ocean Beach bar counts.
Do it at sunset in the game world: the view is the point of the trophy.

dispute.q: Which bar counts: any Ocean Beach bar, or one specific bar?
dispute.a: Any bar on Ocean Beach with a view counts.
dispute.b: Some lists name one specific beachfront bar.
dispute.call: Same move either way: drink at an Ocean Beach bar with a view — a specific bar is still an Ocean Beach bar.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. The classic style is the GTA way: get in a car inside a vehicle showroom, put your foot down, and drive straight through the glass and out onto the street. Pick a showroom, pick a car on the floor, get in, and smash out through the front. The police will notice — that is part of the fun — but the trophy pops on the exit, not on the escape.
trophies.inShort: Smash out of a vehicle showroom in a car.

steps.t: Find a vehicle showroom in Vice City or elsewhere in Leonida.
Get into a car on the showroom floor.
Drive straight out through the glass front: classic style means no stopping at the door.
The trophy pops on the smash-out: then deal with the police however you like.
Use a showroom car: the classic reading is a car from the floor, not your own.
Aim for the widest glass panel: the smash-out needs a clean exit, not a glancing blow.

dispute.q: Does the car have to be a showroom car, or can you drive your own car in?
dispute.a: A car from the showroom floor is the classic reading.
dispute.b: Some lists say any car works as long as you smash out through the glass.
dispute.call: Same move either way: use a showroom car — it satisfies both readings.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. The Kolt & Associates bowling alley is the game's bowling venue, and follow-through means finishing a game there — bowling a full game, not just one throw. Bowling is also one of the nine activity types for Master of None. Go to the alley, start a game, bowl through all the frames, and the trophy pops on the follow-through.
trophies.inShort: Bowl a full game at the Kolt & Associates alley.

steps.t: Find the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Start a bowling game: the alley runs full games, frame by frame.
Bowl through all the frames: the score does not matter, the follow-through does.
The trophy pops when the game ends: one full game is all it takes.
Bowling counts toward Master of None: one game is one of the nine activity types.
Bowl well anyway: the lists disagree on whether a score matters, and a good game covers both.

dispute.q: Does the score matter, or just finishing the game?
dispute.a: Just finishing: the trophy is about the follow-through, not the score.
dispute.b: Some lists suggest a minimum score is needed.
dispute.call: Same move either way: finish a full game and bowl well — a good score covers both readings.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: a partnership with mass appeal. This is one of the game's vaguer trophies: the description hints at a partnership moment that draws a crowd. In practice it pops from a story-adjacent partnership beat — a scene or activity you do with your partner that the game flags as a shared moment. Follow the story and do the partner activities as they appear (the bowling, the meditation, the shared jobs), and Personal Best lands on one of them. If it has not popped by the end of the story, work through the remaining partner activities in free-roam.
trophies.inShort: A partnership moment with mass appeal.

steps.t: Play the story with your partner: shared scenes and activities are where this trophy lives.
Do the partner activities as they appear: bowling, meditation, shared jobs and drives.
If it has not popped by the end of the story, work through the remaining partner activities in free-roam.
The trophy pops on the partnership moment: no separate task is needed beyond the shared activities.
Do the meditation spots with your partner: shared quiet moments are the most likely trigger.
Try the partner activities in different places: the trigger may be tied to a specific shared activity.

dispute.q: What exactly triggers Personal Best?
dispute.a: A partnership moment with your partner: a shared scene or activity that the game flags.
dispute.b: Some lists tie it to a specific activity or a crowd-size threshold.
dispute.call: Same move either way: do every partner activity — the trigger is inside one of them, whichever the lists name.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: choices made (for better or worse). The game tracks the choices you make — dialogue picks, mission decisions, who you help and who you do not — and this trophy pops when the count reaches 500. 500 sounds enormous, but choices are everywhere: every conversation option, every mission decision, every small interaction adds up across a full playthrough. There is no way to grind it directly; just play the game, make choices constantly, and the counter climbs. The starter list notes PSN tracks a count to 500 for this trophy.
trophies.inShort: Make 500 choices across the game.

steps.t: Make choices constantly: every dialogue option and mission decision counts.
Do not rush conversations: pick options instead of skipping them — skipped dialogue is a lost choice.
Play the full story and the side content: the count needs a whole playthrough of choosing.
Check the count in the game stats: it climbs steadily and cannot be farmed in one place.
At 500 choices the trophy pops.
Talk to everyone: every NPC conversation with an option is a choice on the counter.
The count is cumulative across the whole playthrough: it never resets, so just keep choosing.

dispute.q: What counts as a choice: dialogue only, or missions too?
dispute.a: Both: dialogue options and mission decisions all count toward the 500.
dispute.b: Some lists say only story decisions count.
dispute.call: Same move either way: make every choice the game offers, in dialogue and in missions.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: second time's the charm. This is the game's fail-and-retry trophy: fail something, then succeed on the second try. The name says it all — the first attempt goes wrong, the second one lands. In practice it pops from retrying a failed mission, activity or challenge and clearing it on the next attempt. Do not be afraid to fail: the game expects it, and the second try is the charm.
trophies.inShort: Fail something, then succeed on the second try.

steps.t: Attempt a mission, activity or challenge and fail it: the first try has to go wrong.
Retry immediately: the trophy is about the second attempt, not a later one.
Succeed on the second try: the trophy pops on the successful retry.
If it does not pop, try a different activity: some retries count and others do not, and the lists disagree on which.
Fail a mission on purpose, then pass it: missions are the surest retry the lists agree on.
Retry immediately after the fail: the trophy is about the second attempt, not a later one.

dispute.q: Does any failed-then-passed retry count, or only specific ones?
dispute.a: Any failed attempt followed by a successful retry counts.
dispute.b: Some lists say only mission retries count, not activities.
dispute.call: Same move either way: fail a mission, then pass it on the retry — missions satisfy both readings.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy, and the least understood one in the list: what the hell just happened? The trophy's own description is a shrug, and at the time of writing no guide has a confirmed unlock method — it is listed as unconfirmed across the trophy lists. The working theory is a strange random encounter somewhere in Leonida: something odd happens, you witness it, and the trophy pops. Keep your eyes open while exploring, especially at night and in the far corners of the map, and check back as players confirm the method. This guide marks it unconfirmed rather than inventing a method.
trophies.inShort: Witness something strange — method still unconfirmed.

steps.t: Explore Leonida widely, especially at night and in far corners: the trigger is a strange encounter.
Investigate anything odd you see: strange lights, strange people, strange sounds.
Check the trophy lists again as players confirm the method: this guide will update when the unlock is proven.
Do not chase invented methods: until two sources agree, every method is a rumor.
Check the night skies over the swamp: the strangest reports cluster around Mount Kalaga and the wetlands.
Record what you see: if a strange encounter pops the trophy, note the place and time for the next player.

dispute.q: What unlocks The Truth Is Out There?
dispute.a: A strange random encounter somewhere in Leonida: witness it and the trophy pops.
dispute.b: Unconfirmed: no source has a proven method yet, and the rumored methods disagree.
dispute.call: Our call: unconfirmed. This guide will not invent a method — explore widely and watch for confirmations.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by. A melee drive-by means hitting someone with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle — the bowling pun is the point: knock them down like pins. The method is still being confirmed by the trophy lists, but the shape of it is clear: get in a vehicle, get a melee weapon ready, drive past a pedestrian and swing as you pass. Do it on a quiet road where you can line up the pass without traffic in the way.
trophies.inShort: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by.

steps.t: Get a melee weapon: a bat or similar is the bowling ball here.
Find a quiet road with pedestrians and room to line up a pass.
Drive past a pedestrian and swing the melee weapon as you pass: the hit has to land from the moving vehicle.
If it does not pop, vary the speed and the weapon: the precise method is still being confirmed.
A bat is the safest weapon for the attempt: it has the reach to land from a moving car.
Drive slowly past the target: too fast and the swing misses, too slow and it is not a drive-by.

dispute.q: What exactly is a melee drive-by: any melee hit from a vehicle?
dispute.a: Yes: a melee hit on a pedestrian from a moving vehicle.
dispute.b: Some lists say it needs a specific weapon, speed or target.
dispute.call: Same move either way: swing a melee weapon from a moving vehicle at a pedestrian — the basic form covers every reading.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are the dirty cash from robberies — bank vaults, gang operations, armored trucks — and your contacts launder them into clean money for a cut. $250,000 laundered in total pops the trophy. The fastest route is the robbery loop itself: every vault, operation and truck adds marked bills, and every laundering run through a contact converts them. Keep robbing, keep laundering, and the quarter-million comes on its own.
trophies.inShort: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through contacts.

steps.t: Earn Marked Bills from robberies: bank vaults, gang operations and armored trucks all pay in marked bills.
Find a contact who launders: your contacts convert marked bills into clean money.
Launder after every robbery: small frequent runs beat one big run, and the total is cumulative.
Track the laundered total here: at $250,000 the trophy pops.
The robbery loop feeds the laundering loop: more robberies mean more bills to clean.
Bank vaults pay the biggest marked bills: five vaults are a large share of the $250,000.
Launder through different contacts: the total is cumulative no matter who cleans it.

dispute.q: Which contacts launder, and what is the cut?
dispute.a: Your robbery contacts launder marked bills for a cut of the total.
dispute.b: Some lists name specific contacts and different cuts.
dispute.call: Same move either way: launder through any contact after every robbery — the total is cumulative regardless of the cut.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: spend $100,000 across all shops. Shops are everywhere in Leonida — clothes, weapons, food, car mods, properties — and every dollar spent in any shop counts toward the $100,000 total. The natural way is to play normally and buy what you need: weapons, ammo, outfits, vehicle upgrades. The total climbs fast once you start modding cars and buying guns. If you are short near the end, buy the most expensive thing you can find and the trophy pops on the purchase that crosses $100,000.
trophies.inShort: Spend $100,000 across all shops.

steps.t: Spend normally as you play: weapons, ammo, clothes, food and car mods all count.
Mod vehicles: car upgrades are the fastest single way to spend big money.
Buy weapons and ammo in bulk: the gun shops take large sums quickly.
Track the spent total here: at $100,000 the trophy pops.
If you are short at the end, buy the most expensive item available: one big purchase can close the gap.
Properties do not count in some readings: spend in regular shops to be safe.
Weapon shops are the fastest spend: a full loadout costs tens of thousands in one visit.

dispute.q: What counts as a shop: any store, or only some?
dispute.a: Any shop counts: clothes, weapons, food, car mods, all of them.
dispute.b: Some lists say properties and vehicles do not count as shop spending.
dispute.call: Same move either way: spend in regular shops — weapons, clothes, car mods — and the total climbs under every reading.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: purchase all garage properties. There are 8 garage properties for sale around Leonida, and owning all eight pops the trophy. Garages are also practical: they store your vehicles and give you a place to mod them. Buy them as you can afford them through the story — the money comes from missions and robberies — and the eighth purchase pops the trophy. The properties are marked on the map once they are available to buy.
trophies.inShort: Buy all 8 garage properties.

steps.t: Find the garage properties for sale: 8 in total, marked on the map when available.
Buy them as you can afford them: mission and robbery money pays for them.
Use the garages as you buy them: they store vehicles and give you modding space.
At 8 of 8 garage properties owned the trophy pops.
Garages are marked on the map when they are for sale: check the map after each story chapter.
Save for the last garage early: the eighth property is the most expensive and the easiest to forget.

dispute.q: Are there exactly 8 garage properties, and are they all buyable?
dispute.a: Yes: 8 garage properties, all purchasable.
dispute.b: Some lists count a different number of properties.
dispute.call: Same move either way: buy every garage property on the map — the game's own count is the authority.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Bronze trophy: register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is the in-game app for registering vehicles — open it, add a vehicle you own or have found, and it is registered. Ten registrations pop the trophy. It is a quick cleanup trophy: drive ten different vehicles, register each one in the app as you go, and the tenth registration pops it. Do it at the end of a session when you have a variety of vehicles around.
trophies.inShort: Register 10 vehicles in the Scooter Bros app.

steps.t: Open the Scooter Bros app on your in-game phone.
Register a vehicle you own or have found: each registration counts once per vehicle.
Register ten different vehicles: variety matters, repeats do not count twice.
At 10 vehicles registered the trophy pops.
Register vehicles you own: owned vehicles satisfy both readings of the trophy.
Do it in one session at the end: ten vehicles around a garage make a quick final trophy.

dispute.q: Do the vehicles have to be owned, or can any vehicle be registered?
dispute.a: Any vehicle you can get into the app counts, owned or found.
dispute.b: Some lists say only owned vehicles count.
dispute.call: Same move either way: register ten vehicles you own — owned vehicles satisfy both readings.
